oewn-00721658-v.learner: to think of something as probable or likely.
examples: she began to declare that it was what she had expected all the while
Mr. Gardiner himself did not expect any success from this measure

oewn-00721987-v.learner: to wait for something that will probably happen.
examples: the two who were most anxiously expected, to the credit of their punctuality as sportsmen, were in very good time

oewn-00757790-v.learner: to treat something as a duty that someone owes, and to ask for it and count on getting it.
examples: She expects her pupils to hand in their work on Friday.

oewn-07558676-n.learner: a strong good feeling of caring about someone or something and holding them dear.
examples: Their love for their children was plain in everything they did.

oewn-07503480-n.learner: a deep feeling of wanting someone and being pulled towards them in a sexual way.
examples: A lady's imagination is very rapid; it jumps from admiration to love, from love to matrimony, in a moment.

oewn-09869006-n.learner: a person who is loved, and a name you call that person.
examples: Come here, my love, and sit by the fire.

connotation.why: names the person with open fondness instead of neutrally

oewn-00803980-v.learner: to agree to something and give someone permission for it.
examples: Only let me assure you, my dear Miss Elizabeth, that I can from my heart most cordially wish you equal felicity in marriage.
let me persuade you to follow my example, and take a turn about the room

oewn-02427979-v.learner: to make it possible for something to happen, by doing one thing or by doing nothing.
examples: as for wedding clothes, do not let them wait for that
He said nothing and let the mistake stand.

oewn-00773535-v.learner: to make something happen on purpose.
examples: She let it be known that she would not come.

oewn-09842904-n.learner: your father's sister or your mother's sister, or the wife of your uncle.
examples: Jane ran to her uncle and aunt, and welcomed and thanked them both, with alternate smiles and tears.
"My dear aunt, this is being serious indeed."

oewn-15271664-n.learner: a short stretch of time, with no set length.
examples: He sat down for a few moments, and then getting up walked about the room.
Whatever can give his sister any pleasure, is sure to be done in a moment.
From the moment he entered the room, she knew something was wrong.

oewn-15144992-n.learner: the time that is happening now.
examples: She is not at home at the moment.
At that moment they were met from another walk by Mrs. Hurst and Elizabeth herself.

oewn-02026650-v.learner: to come together with someone because you planned it, or to be there when someone arrives.
examples: My uncle and aunt and I were to go together; and the others were to meet us at the church.

oewn-02602110-v.learner: to come to know someone for the first time.
examples: They first met at a ball, and he barely spoke to her.

oewn-06297048-n.learner: a single piece of language that people who speak that language can pick out.
examples: I am not so certain that I should myself use the word "narrow" in connection with her.

oewn-06750911-n.learner: a short thing that someone says.
examples: You know, sister, we agreed long ago never to mention a word about it.
you will find me as good as my word

oewn-15190336-n.learner: the part of the day between first light and midday.
examples: she was tempted, by the pleasantness of the morning, to stop at the gates and look into the park
I thought Miss Elizabeth Bennet looked remarkably well when she came into the room this morning.

oewn-15193837-n.learner: the first light of the day.
examples: The sky was already pale when morning came over the fields.

oewn-06645178-n.learner: a set phrase you say when you greet someone or leave them, to wish them a good morning.
examples: "Morning," he said, and went on down the lane.

oewn-10146810-n.learner: a man with polished manners and refined ways.
examples: He danced only four dances, though gentlemen were scarce
when the gentlemen entered, Jane was no longer the first object

connotation.why: praises the man's manners rather than just naming him a man

oewn-10765000-n.learner: a male servant who looks after the personal needs of the man he works for.
examples: He travelled with his gentleman, who saw to his clothes and his shaving.

oewn-09895920-n.learner: a boy or man who has the same parents as you.
examples: Miss Bingley is to live with her brother, and keep his house
Her brother's recommendation was enough to insure her favour

oewn-09896358-n.learner: a man who belongs to the same club, religion, or other group as you.
examples: Every man who joins the order is a brother to the rest.

oewn-09896590-n.learner: a word you use when you speak to a man who works for the same cause as you.
examples: Stand with us, brother, and the strike will hold.

connotation.why: claims warm fellowship with the man addressed
